GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2012-06-19T00:26:58Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: ray.intersectObject(s) requires intersected objects to be in the scene.
Description: I am not sure this is a bug, but I have a use case where I have a rectangular plane made of many (~50x50) rectangular tiles.  I want to do the standard intersection of a ray to determine human interaction.  

To avoid intersecting my ray with hundreds of rectangles, I wanted to compute the intersection with the larger rectangle (not rendered or actually part of the scene).  

I discovered that unless the rectangle was part of the scene, ray.intersectObject will not return an intersecting object!

REASONING: This issue is about the behavior of the ray.intersectObject(s) method in Three.js, which requires objects to be part of the scene to detect intersections. This is a conceptual issue about how the library works rather than a bug that needs to be fixed through code changes. 

The issue can be verified without a build environment by:
1. Reviewing the Three.js documentation to confirm the expected behavior of ray.intersectObject
2. Understanding that the ray intersection functionality requires objects to be in the scene graph to work properly
3. Analyzing the code logic without needing to run it

The solution would likely involve either adding the larger rectangle to the scene (perhaps with visibility set to false), using a different approach for ray intersection, or understanding that this is the intended behavior of the library. All of these can be verified through documentation review and code analysis without needing to build and run the code.
